CMB-021 (PMC6426203 re-read 2026-10-29): Table 3 "Agreement in percent body fat estimates compared to dual-emission X-ray absorptiometry", all seven rows (DXA minus method in points, 90% CI, MAPE): hydrostatic weighing 1.0 (0.6-1.4) 13.4%; skinfold thickness 1.4 (1.1-1.7) 11.7%; ADP 1.6 (1.3-1.9) 14.5%; IR 4.2 (3.7-4.7) 18.7%; Omron BIA 4.9 (4.5-5.3) 21.9%; Tanita BIA 3.5 (3.0-4.0) 17.2%; Valhalla BIA 1.6 (1.1-2.1) 17.0%. 10% equivalence interval -2.7 to 2.7 ("+/- 10% of the criterion mean, which corresponded to +/- 2.7% body fat"): hydrostatic weighing, skinfolds, ADP and Valhalla BIA equivalent; at 15% "all surrogate assessments, except for Omron BIA and IR". Table 1: DXA 27.0% (SD 7.6) overall (its women and men rows, 28.2 and 20.8, do not average to it with 301 and 136: not used). Table 4: "differences between DXA and each surrogate assessment increased as mean percent body fat increased", all but Valhalla BIA (r = 0.04, p = 0.784). Devices: DXA Hologic Discovery W (software 12.1); BOD POD (COSMED), seated, two volume measurements; Futrex-6100 A/ZL light wand on the belly of the biceps; OMRON HBF-306 handheld, arms extended; Tanita BF-556 two-electrode foot-to-foot scale; Valhalla Scientific Model 1990B, four electrodes on the right hand and foot, supine; hydrostatic weighing on an underwater swing after full exhalation. Pre-test: large meals avoided 2 hours, vigorous exercise 12 hours, alcohol 48 hours, liquids limited to 2 glasses of water at least 2 hours before, bladder emptied immediately before; "dehydration can lead to overestimation of percent body fat", "overhydration can lead to underestimation". sample_note: Chat read the full text (2026-11-07). Table 1: Devine (1974) men 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 feet, women 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg; Robinson et al. Quotes: "The equations were provided by Devine (Table 1) to calculate creatinine clearance given the argument that it would be a better estimate of gentamicin clearance"; "the equations were not referenced to a particular data set, and so created a controversy over their validity"; Robinson et al. determined that they "were based on the empiric estimates of his mentor, Dr. Margaret McCarron"; Devine's equations are a kilogram version of a simple rule developed empirically from height-weight tables: "For women, allow 100 lbs. for the first 5 feet and 5 lbs. for each additional inch. For men, allow 110 lbs. for the first 5 feet and 5 lbs. for each additional inch."; "In addition, a 10% variation above or below the calculated weight was allowed for individual differences." (this sentence belongs to that rule, not to frame size); "Since 1974, more than 200 articles have cited the equation for lean/'ideal' body weight as published by Devine."; frame sizes in the early tables "were not defined and were left to the subjective judgment of the examiner"; "Body frame was later defined and published in the 1959 Metropolitan Desirable Weight Table"; the equations of Robinson et al. and Miller et al.
